title: Countably generated module freeness criterion
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module generated by an at most countable subset, meaning that every element is a finite $R$-linear combination of that subset. Suppose that for every pair of submodules $N,F\subseteq M$ such that the addition map $N\oplus F\to M$ is an isomorphism and $F$ has a finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module], every element $x\in N$ belongs to a free direct summand of $N$: there exist submodules $G,H\subseteq N$ with $N=G\oplus H$, $x\in G$, and $G$ free. Then $M$ is free. In these decompositions $N\oplus F$ and $G\oplus H$ mean the modules of pairs, and each direct-sum assertion means uniqueness of the expression as a sum of one element of each submodule.

proof.text: Choose a sequence of generators $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ for $M$, repeating elements or inserting $0$ if the original generating subset is finite. The hypothesis that an at most countable subset generates $M$ gives such a sequence, and every element of $M$ is a finite linear combination of its terms.

source.place: Tag 0591, lemma-freeness-criteria, proof: first sentence ('Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots$ be a countable set of generators')

proof.text: Inductively suppose finite free direct summands $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ have been chosen so that $S_n=F_1\oplus\cdots\oplus F_n$ is a direct summand of $M$ containing $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. Write $M=S_n\oplus N$ and let $x\in N$ be the $N$-component of $x_{n+1}$. The finite direct sum $S_n$ has a finite basis obtained by taking the union of finite bases of the $F_i$, so the assumed criterion applies to the decomposition $M=N\oplus S_n$. It gives submodules $G,H\subseteq N$ with $N=G\oplus H$, $x\in G$, and $G$ free.

source.place: Tag 0591, lemma-freeness-criteria, proof: inductive construction of $F_1, F_2, \ldots$ and the paragraph beginning 'Namely, given $F_1, \ldots, F_n$'

proof.text: Choose a basis of the free module $G$. The element $x$ has finite support in this basis; let $F_{n+1}$ be the span of the finitely many basis vectors in that support (and include any additional basis vectors if needed). The complementary basis vectors give $G=F_{n+1}\oplus G'$, with $F_{n+1}$ finite free. Together with $N=G\oplus H$ and $M=S_n\oplus N$, this exhibits $F_{n+1}$ as a finite free direct summand of $M$ containing $x$, and it makes $S_{n+1}=S_n\oplus F_{n+1}$ a direct summand containing $x_1,\ldots,x_{n+1}$ because $x_{n+1}$ is the sum of its $S_n$-component and $x$.

source.place: Tag 0591, lemma-freeness-criteria, proof: 'Of course we can replace $F_{n+1}$ by a finite free direct summand of $F_{n+1}$'

proof.text: The induction supplies $S_n=F_1\oplus\cdots\oplus F_n$ for every $n$, and each generator $x_j$ lies in $S_j$. Hence every element of $M$, being a finite linear combination of the $x_j$, lies in some $S_n$. The direct-sum uniqueness at each finite stage implies that the sum $M=\bigoplus_{i\ge1}F_i$ is direct: a finite relation is contained in one $S_n$ and all its components vanish there.

source.place: Tag 0591, lemma-freeness-criteria, proof: conclusion of the inductive construction before 'Then $M = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^{\infty} F_i$ is free'

proof.text: For each $F_i$ choose its finite basis. The disjoint union of these bases is a basis of $\bigoplus_{i\ge1}F_i$: a vector has finite support in the outer direct sum and finite basis support in each of those finitely many coordinates, while uniqueness follows coordinatewise. Since this direct sum equals $M$, the module $M$ is free.

source.place: Tag 0591, lemma-freeness-criteria, proof: final sentence 'Then $M = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^{\infty} F_i$ is free'

lean.statement: theorem free_of_countable_generators_of_free_summands {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (hcountable : ∃ s : Set M, s.Countable ∧ Submodule.span R s = ⊤) (hsummands : ∀ (N F : Submodule R M), IsCompl N F → (∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin n) R F)) → ∀ x : N, ∃ G H : Submodule R N, IsCompl G H ∧ x ∈ G ∧ Module.Free R G) : Module.Free R M
